# Gauteng

URL: /gauteng
Page title: Explore Gauteng: regions, cities & neighbourhoods | Property Listify
Meta description: Understand Gauteng’s three metros and two districts. Compare Johannesburg, Tshwane, Ekurhuleni, West Rand and Sedibeng, then explore their city guides.
Status: published
Sources checked: 2026-10-15

### Introduction

One province, many ways to live. Get your bearings in Johannesburg, the greater Pretoria area and the East Rand, then look west to the towns of the West Rand or south towards the Vaal. Start with the region that fits your everyday life, and explore its places in more detail.

### Johannesburg (Metropolitan municipality)

_A city of distinct neighbourhoods_

From the inner city and Soweto to Sandton, Randburg and Midrand, “Joburg” is much more than one property market.

The City of Johannesburg is divided into seven municipal regions. Its inner city, northern business centres, western neighbourhoods and southern communities sit within the same metro, but they are different starting points for a home search. A Johannesburg address alone tells you very little about the journey you will make each day.

Start by identifying the part of the city you need to reach. Sandton and Rosebank are useful points of reference along the Gautrain corridor; Midrand lies further north, while Roodepoort and Soweto offer different western and south-western contexts. “Johannesburg North” is a familiar area description, rather than a single municipality or a precise search boundary.

**What to weigh up:** Compare specific neighbourhoods around your daily destination. A citywide result is useful for browsing, but it should not decide your commute for you.

Places named: Johannesburg, Randburg, Midrand, Roodepoort, Soweto

Sources: joburg, gautrain

### Tshwane & Pretoria (Metropolitan municipality)

_Look beyond a Pretoria address_

Pretoria, Centurion and the metro’s northern and eastern communities belong to a much wider Tshwane geography.

Pretoria and the City of Tshwane are not interchangeable geographic scopes. Tshwane’s seven service regions cover Pretoria and Centurion as well as communities extending north and east. A guide to Pretoria can help you understand the city, but it should not be treated as a guide to every place in the metro.

Centurion is a separate place to explore between Johannesburg and Pretoria. Within Pretoria, compare the centre with the neighbourhoods on the side of the city you need. Further east, Bronkhorstspruit sits in Tshwane’s Region 7. Gautrain connects Centurion, Pretoria and Hatfield, but a station on the network does not mean every home is within walking distance.

**What to weigh up:** Shortlist around your campus, workplace or regular destination first. Check the full trip, including the distance from the station or main road to the property.

Places named: Pretoria, Centurion, Bronkhorstspruit

Sources: tshwane, tshwane-east, gautrain

### Ekurhuleni (Metropolitan municipality)

_Get to know the East Rand town by town_

An interconnected network of towns, with airport, industrial and residential settings that vary considerably by location.

Ekurhuleni brings together nine established towns: Alberton, Benoni, Boksburg, Brakpan, Edenvale, Germiston, Kempton Park, Nigel and Springs. The familiar name “East Rand” helps with orientation, but a town and a metropolitan municipality are different levels of geography.

OR Tambo International Airport is an important reference point for the northern part of the metro. The mining-belt towns stretch eastwards, while Alberton provides a southern starting point. Rather than treating the whole metro as one shortlist, compare the town, the neighbourhood and its connection to your daily destinations. Airport access, proximity to employment and a residential street’s surroundings are separate considerations.

**What to weigh up:** Use an individual town as your next step. If airport access matters, check the actual route and property surroundings rather than relying on the “East Rand” label.

Places named: Benoni, Boksburg, Alberton, Kempton Park, Germiston

Sources: ekurhuleni, gautrain

### West Rand (District municipality)

_Towns, open landscapes and a different western context_

A district beyond Johannesburg’s western neighbourhoods, bringing together Mogale City, Rand West City and Merafong City.

The West Rand district has three local municipalities: Mogale City, Rand West City and Merafong City. Krugersdorp, Randfontein and Carletonville are useful town-level starting points. The district also includes places such as Magaliesburg and Fochville, so “West Rand” should not be read as one continuous suburban neighbourhood.

It is also important to distinguish the district from the western side of Johannesburg: Roodepoort belongs to the Johannesburg metro. When comparing western locations, begin with the town and then the specific neighbourhood or property setting. A town address, a smallholding and a rural property can involve quite different access and service arrangements.

**What to weigh up:** For a smallholding or rural property, ask about land use, road access, water, electricity and maintenance responsibilities before comparing it with a suburban home.

Places named: Krugersdorp, Randfontein, Carletonville, Magaliesburg

Sources: west-rand, joburg

### Sedibeng & the Vaal (District municipality)

_Southern Gauteng, with more than one local rhythm_

Vereeniging, Vanderbijlpark, Meyerton and Heidelberg provide different ways into the south of the province.

Sedibeng is the southern Gauteng district made up of Emfuleni, Midvaal and Lesedi. The river communities around Vereeniging and Vanderbijlpark, the Meyerton area and Heidelberg are distinct places to explore. The R59, N1 and N3 provide different regional connections; choose the relevant corridor rather than assuming that every address has the same access to Johannesburg.

“The Vaal” is a familiar regional description, not a synonym for one municipal boundary. The wider river region also connects to places outside Gauteng, including Sasolburg in the Free State. This province guide keeps its place links within Gauteng. For a river or dam-side property, check the exact address and municipality as well as access, services and any property-specific restrictions.

**What to weigh up:** Decide whether you want a town neighbourhood, a smaller settlement or a waterside setting. Then investigate that location on its own terms.

Places named: Vereeniging, Vanderbijlpark, Meyerton, Heidelberg

Sources: sedibeng, metsimaholo

### Everyday life

**Start with the journey you make most**

Gautrain links Johannesburg, Sandton, Midrand, Centurion, Pretoria and Hatfield, with an airport connection. It is one part of a wider transport picture. Check current routes and service information with the operator, and test your full door-to-door trip at the times you expect to travel. Distance on a map is not a travel-time promise.

Sources: gautrain

**Compare the neighbourhood, not just the region**

A metro label cannot tell you whether a particular home fits your routine. Mark the schools, healthcare facilities, shops and regular destinations you need, then investigate the neighbourhood around each shortlisted property. Confirm admissions, services and opening arrangements with the relevant provider rather than assuming proximity guarantees access.

Sources: none

**Look at the home and its running costs**

When comparing apartments, townhouses, freestanding homes or smallholdings, ask about the costs and responsibilities attached to that specific property. Levies, rates, utilities, maintenance and applicable rules can change the practical comparison. A lower asking price alone does not establish a lower cost of living.

Sources: none

### Questions

**Is Pretoria the same place as Tshwane?**

No. Pretoria is a city within the City of Tshwane metropolitan municipality. Tshwane covers a wider area, including Centurion and communities further north and east. Choose a Pretoria guide for city context, then narrow to the neighbourhood you mean.

**Does a Johannesburg search mean the northern suburbs?**

It should not. Johannesburg includes the inner city, Soweto, western and southern areas as well as northern neighbourhoods. Names such as “Johannesburg North” need more precise place choices before they can define a useful home search.

**Is the West Rand part of Johannesburg?**

The West Rand district is separate from the Johannesburg metro. Roodepoort is within Johannesburg, while places such as Krugersdorp, Randfontein and Carletonville are in the West Rand district. Everyday regional labels can be broader than administrative boundaries.

**Can this guide tell me where lofts or townhouses are most common?**

The city guides are a starting point for exploring neighbourhoods. A reliable property-type comparison needs enough correctly classified listings within defined areas. We do not infer the province’s housing stock or demand from a small selection of listings.

**Are listing prices the same as sale prices?**

No. An advertised asking price is the seller’s or landlord’s request, rather than a completed transaction. Property Listify inventory counts describe listings available on this platform, not all homes in the province. This guide does not currently publish regional price estimates or price-growth claims.

### Introduction

Johannesburg is a collection of very different places. Start with the part of the city that fits your everyday destinations, then get to know its neighbourhoods. A Sandton address, an inner-city apartment and a home in Soweto can mean very different daily journeys.

### Collection: Across the city

Five starting points for getting your bearings across the wider Johannesburg metro.

The municipal metro and the places in our catalogue are different levels of geography. Each verified guide has its own place scope; opening one does not silently combine its properties with Johannesburg’s results.

### Collection: Green spaces

Start with a park or garden, then investigate the neighbourhood around it.

City Parks identifies the Botanical Garden in Emmarentia, Zoo Lake in Parkview, Delta Park in Blairgowrie and Klipriviersburg Nature Reserve in Kibler Park. Check each venue’s current access arrangements and the actual route from a property. Collection membership is not a safety rating or a promise of walking distance.

Places: Emmarentia (Johannesburg Botanical Garden & dam); Parkview (Zoo Lake as a local reference point); Blairgowrie (Explore around Delta Park); Kibler Park (Klipriviersburg Nature Reserve)

### Collection: Rail connections

Use a station as a starting point for a more practical neighbourhood shortlist.

Park, Rosebank, Sandton and Midrand are Gautrain commuter-network reference points. The station is only part of a journey: compare the walk, feeder connection or drive at both ends. A city-guide link does not mean every home is close to its station.

Places: Rosebank (Compare the area around Rosebank station); Sandton (Explore around the Sandton node); Midrand (Investigate your full station connection); Braamfontein (Investigate connections around Park station)

Sources: rail, rosebank

### Collection: Neighbourhood life

Look closer at individual neighbourhoods before deciding where to search.

Use these places as starting points for your own comparison. Check the street, housing arrangement, daily services and regular destinations. They are not ranked for affordability, school quality, safety or investment returns.

Places: Rosebank (Compare the neighbourhood, not just the node); Emmarentia (Explore the streets around the garden); Parkview (Investigate your everyday local routes); Alexandra (A different northern-city context)

Sources: regions, parks

### Region A · Midrand and the north

Midrand, Diepsloot and Ivory Park are northern reference points. The same municipal region includes quite different neighbourhoods and housing settings.

**What to weigh up:** Start with the destination you need to reach. Compare the specific neighbourhood and the complete route rather than assuming that a northern address means a short commute.

Places named: Midrand, Diepsloot, Ivory Park

### Region B · Randburg and the park neighbourhoods

Northcliff and parts of Randburg, Sandton and Rosebank form this part of the metro. Familiar place names can cross the city’s administrative divisions.

**What to weigh up:** Look at a specific neighbourhood around your regular destinations. A park or business-node name is a useful reference point, but it does not describe every street around it.

Places named: Randburg, Northcliff, Emmarentia

### Region C · Roodepoort and the west

Roodepoort and parts of Randburg sit on the western side of Johannesburg. This municipal region is distinct from Gauteng’s West Rand district.

**What to weigh up:** Check which place and municipality the address belongs to. Keep a Roodepoort shortlist separate from a district-wide search around Krugersdorp or Randfontein.

Places named: Roodepoort, Florida, Roodekrans

### Region D · Soweto

Soweto, including areas such as Diepkloof and Meadowlands, provides a south-western starting point. Explore its neighbourhoods individually.

**What to weigh up:** Choose a neighbourhood around the routes, services and everyday destinations that matter to you. A Soweto-wide label is orientation, not a substitute for a local guide.

Places named: Soweto, Diepkloof, Meadowlands

### Region E · Sandton and Alexandra

Alexandra and parts of Sandton and Rosebank sit within Region E. An administrative grouping is not a single housing market or one lifestyle.

**What to weigh up:** Compare the exact neighbourhood and property setting. If a rail connection matters, check the route to the station as well as the onward trip.

Places named: Sandton, Alexandra, Rosebank

### Region F · Inner city and Johannesburg South

The inner city and Johannesburg South share a municipal region while offering different urban and residential contexts.

**What to weigh up:** Distinguish a central apartment from a southern neighbourhood home. Compare the building’s running costs and management arrangements alongside your regular journeys.

Places named: Johannesburg, Braamfontein, Kibler Park

### Region G · Lenasia and the deep south

Lenasia, Ennerdale, Orange Farm and Eldorado Park are reference points for the metro’s southern reach.

**What to weigh up:** Check the actual route, access and nearby services for the specific address. Do not assume that the entire metro has the same connection to central Johannesburg.

Places named: Lenasia, Ennerdale, Orange Farm

### Everyday life

**Start with your regular journey**

Work backwards from work, study or family commitments. Check the complete route at the times you actually travel. A station or main road nearby is one part of the decision; the trip at either end still matters.

**Look beyond the property price**

When comparing apartments, townhouses and freestanding homes, ask about levies, rates, utilities, maintenance and building management. Keep sale prices and monthly rents separate. A low asking price alone does not tell you the total cost of living there.

Compare the street, local services and access arrangements with your own needs. Confirm schools, healthcare and transport directly with providers. A metro overview cannot verify an individual home’s surroundings or guarantee access.

### Questions

**Does Johannesburg mean the entire metropolitan municipality?**

Not always. The municipality includes places such as Midrand, Roodepoort and Soweto, while the platform also has separate catalogued city identities. This guide explains the wider context. Live inventory figures and search handoffs use the exact selected catalogue identity, not an inferred municipal boundary.

**Can I explore a suburb before choosing Buy or Rent?**

Yes. Suburb-guide links remain part of the discovery journey. Choose Buy or Rent only when you want property results. Your selected area is shown before you continue.

**Why are there no neighbourhood price rankings?**

Current listings alone do not establish fair value, achieved sale prices or demand. A defensible comparison needs matching property types, transactions, geographic scope and enough priced observations. Unsupported price comparisons are omitted.

**Are the lifestyle collections recommendations for every property?**

No. They identify places and reference points worth investigating. They do not rate neighbourhood safety, promise a commute time or imply that every property is near a park or station.
